content: WS auth (websocket.org guide): browser WebSocket ctor accepts ONLY url+subprotocols - no Authorization header possible (by design); patterns: (a) short-lived token in URL query verified at upgrade - cheap rejection pre-connection but token lands in access logs/history/Referer, mitigate with 5-15min TTL, never long-lived creds; (b) Cookie auth same-origin - inherits session but REQUIRES Origin check on every upgrade (CSRF); (c) first-message auth - token not in logs but unauthenticated connections consume resources => 5s auth timeout + per-IP conn rate limit; long-lived conns need in-band token refresh 30s before expiry; re-check permissions per message not just at connect; always wss. For wesh: one-time single-use ticket minted by authenticated HTTP endpoint, presented in subprotocol or first frame, 5s auth timeout.
